name: Single-organ polyarteritis nodosa

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Adapted criteria for single-organ polyarteritis nodosa

criteria.description: Biopsy demonstrating necrotizing vasculitis of medium-sized arteries confined to a single organ
Clinical manifestations restricted to a single organ system without systemic involvement
Exclusion of systemic polyarteritis nodosa and other systemic vasculitides by clinical and laboratory evaluation
Angiographic evidence of aneurysms or stenoses limited to arteries supplying the affected organ
Elevated inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP) localized to the affected organ

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of necrotizing vasculitis confined to a single organ with clinical localization and exclusion of systemic disease
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires careful exclusion of systemic polyarteritis nodosa and other vasculitides.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Localized necrotizing arteritis in affected organ
searchTerms: localized artery inflammation with tissue death

pathognomonic.symptomName: Organ-specific ischemic manifestations due to medium-vessel involvement
searchTerms: organ damage from medium artery disease
blood vessel blockage causing organ symptoms

common.symptomName: Localized livedo reticularis or skin ulceration
common.notes: If skin is the affected organ

common.symptomName: Localized abdominal pain due to mesenteric artery involvement
searchTerms: localized abdominal pain due to blood flow

common.symptomName: Localized hypertension secondary to renal artery involvement
common.notes: If kidney is the affected organ
searchTerms: high blood pressure from kidney artery issues
localized hypertension due to renal artery
numbness or tingling in one area

rare.notes: If vessels supplying inner ear involved

laboratory: Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and C-reactive protein (CRP)
Normal or mildly elevated antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies (ANCA) - usually negative
Absence of systemic inflammatory markers outside affected organ
imaging: Angiography showing microaneurysms, stenoses, or occlusions limited to arteries supplying the affected organ
MRI or CT demonstrating localized organ ischemia or infarction
genetic: No known specific genetic mutations associated
other: Histopathology showing transmural necrotizing inflammation of medium-sized arteries confined to single organ

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of infectious agents or tumor cells

redFlags: Rapid progression of ischemic organ damage
Development of systemic symptoms (fever, weight loss, malaise)
Signs of systemic vasculitis or multi-organ involvement
references: Jennette JC, Falk RJ, Bacon PA, et al. 2012 Revised International Chapel Hill Consensus Conference Nomenclature of Vasculitides. Arthritis Rheum. 2013;65(1):1-11.
Pagnoux C. Updates in ANCA-associated vasculitis. Eur J Rheumatol. 2016;3(3):122-133.
